newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bucharest bourse set for more giddy gains - IBA.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse set for more giddy gains - IBA.

text.p: Investmentbank Austria said on Wednesday it expects Romania's stock market to stage another heady upswing within two years, adding that the 170 percent surge of the last three months was not an exception but a trend.

"Based on the readiness of the Romanian government to open up its economy to international investors, there will be a further strong upswing of the Romanian market within the next 24 months," said Peter Nowak, a member of the bank's executive board, in a statement.

Investmentbank Austria (IBA), whose Bucharest subsidiary IB Austria Securities is among the top four brokers in Romania in terms of trading volume, also forecasts a doubling of market capitalisation from the current $500 million on the Bucharest bourse and $1.5 billion on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.

IBA said the new 1.5 percent tax on each portfolio transaction, announced two weeks ago, was lower than previously feared and therefore made the bourse more attractive. Earlier proposals set a four percent fee on capital gains repatriation.

"The deciding factor is that the government is not waiting for international investment, but that it is now deliberately promoting it," said Fritz Schweiger, the bank's chief analyst for Central and Eastern Europe.
The 1.5 percent tax "is irrelevant for the medium-term investor", he added.

Schweiger said that while the big enterprises listed on the upper segment of the Bucharest bourse seemed fairly valued, there were numerous investment possibilities on the second section and in new listings.
"We expect about another 80 new listings this year," he said.
Based on prospective earnings for 1997, IBA said the market should currently trade on a price/earnings ratio of 10 times.

But IBA cited a note of caution. "One risk is that at present partly speculative money is flowing into the market and investors could very easily fall smack into a liquidity trap." -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
